entries.official_ci_explanation:
## Official CI follow-up

The official PyTorch job fails in `TestInvariantMetricMatrixSO.test_exp_after_log`. An [isolated replay](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43823522685) reproduces that SO(3) numerical failure on unchanged upstream `2fc8e25` and obtains identical results after applying this PR, using Python 3.13, PyTorch 2.15.0 (CPU), NumPy 2.5.5, and SciPy 1.18.1. Profiling confirms that this calculation never calls the changed NFold source.

The separate NumPy project-coverage check drops from 85.4484% to 85.4375%: comparing the [base coverage log](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/42744796656/job/129594204695) and [this PR's coverage log](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/43818701559/job/133136536401), NFold coverage improves from 115/124 to 118/126 statements, while existing branches in EM, online k-means, PCA, and trees change coverage outside the patch. The changed-line coverage checks pass; the official failing checks remain visible.

### Additional Autograd CI follow-up

The later Autograd failure is `TestBetaMetric.test_inner_product_derivative_matrix_vec`, which raises `ValueError` when an Autograd `ArrayBox` reaches the in-place sparse assignment in symmetric-matrix reconstruction. This also appears in the [official unchanged-base job](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/42744796656/job/129594204622). A [fixed-input replay](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43826682548/job/133162070132) with the current official numerical-library versions produces the same exception on exact base `2fc8e25` and this isolated patch, without calling `nfold_manifold.py`.

official_ci_diagnosis.summary: PyTorch SO(3) exp/log fails identically on exact-base and isolated-patch fixed inputs. Autograd has the base Beta reconstruction ValueError. NumPy project coverage falls despite improved NFold coverage; detailed base/patch tables are in the published note.

entries.official_ci_explanation:
### Official CI follow-up

The Autograd failures are seven `TestMatrixPower` cases in `test_hpd_matrices.py`: inverse membership, inverse round-trips, and tangent round-trips. That fixture samples a power anywhere in (0, 1), so its inverse can raise a well-conditioned HPD matrix to a very large power. A [fixed-input replay](https://github.com/Afloat16/geomstats/actions/runs/43826682548/job/133162069816) with power 0.001 reproduces the NaN inverse-round-trip failure on both exact base `2fc8e25` and this patch using the current official numerical-library versions; neither execution calls `ivp.py`. The original random power was not logged, so this establishes an existing failure mode rather than reproducing the exact original draw. The other six assertions share that fixture; their exact random inputs have not been recovered.

official_ci_diagnosis.summary: Seven Autograd HPD matrix-power assertions fail. A small positive power produces the same NaN inverse on base and patch; the original random power and other six exact failing inputs were not recorded.

official_ci_diagnosis.summary: NumPy von Mises-Fisher mean and AAC graph regression and PyTorch transport norm failures have matching base/patch fixed-input failure modes. Original randomized inputs were not recovered. Official Autograd passes after this symmetric-reconstruction fix.

entries.official_ci_explanation:
### Official CI follow-up

The later [Autograd job](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/43836389278/job/133193952209) fails `TestBetaMetric.test_inner_product_derivative_matrix_vec` when an Autograd `ArrayBox` reaches the in-place sparse assignment in `SymmetricMatrices.matrix_representation`, raising `ValueError: setting an array element with a sequence`. The [official job on unchanged base `2fc8e25`](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/42744796656/job/129594204622) contains the same exception and call chain. That reconstruction is unchanged here and is corrected separately in #2235. This identifies the existing exception path; the jobs did not record their original random parameters.

The [PyTorch job](https://github.com/geomstats/geomstats/actions/runs/43836389278/job/133193952059) fails `TestUnitNormedRowsPLTMatricesPullbackMetric.test_parallel_transport_ivp_transported_is_tangent` and `TestAACRegression.test_fit_and_predict_constant`. The original matrices and graph were not printed. Two deterministic replays therefore record complete inputs from the same fixture definitions, then compare exact base `2fc8e25` with this isolated patch using Python 3.13.18, PyTorch 2.15.0 CPU, NumPy 2.5.5, SciPy 1.18.1, and scikit-learn 1.9.1.

The [transport replay](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43871636636/job/133314061514) returns the same tangency result, `[True, True, True, False]`, on both versions. The transported vectors and endpoints also agree element-for-element, including matching NaNs. The [AAC replay](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43871636636/job/133314061031) returns the same total-space distances, `[0.784986936670632, 0.784986936670632]`, while both quotient-space distances are zero: the graph predictions differ only by vertex permutation.

Call tracing, verified first with an actual IVP positive control, shows that neither failing calculation invokes `numerics/ivp.py`. The replay artifacts retain the full input arrays and results. These comparisons establish existing failure modes and unchanged outputs; they do not claim to recover the original unrecorded random draws. An initial diagnostic run used the wrong callback argument order in its trace positive control; the linked follow-up corrects that diagnostic only, with no change to the candidate.

official_ci_diagnosis.summary: Autograd has the base Beta reconstruction ValueError. Matching-fixture fixed inputs reproduce Torch PLT tangent and AAC constant-graph failures on exact base and isolated patch, with identical full outputs and no calls to ivp.py; tracer positive controls verified. Original random inputs were not logged, so the result establishes the existing failure modes rather than recovering the original draws.
